messages:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — pin metadata field evolution. TL;DR: we need a minimal wire schema that supports soft vs hard pins, tenant overrides, and provenance without exploding fields.

sam: +1 on minimal. main friction is clients and older agent versions. we should aim for compact keys but clear compatibility rules.

kai: propose short names to reduce token overhead: `p` (pin type: hard|soft), `l` (lease until ISO ts), `o` (origin/provenance), `h` (hints array). keep semantics explicit in docs.

rachel: concerned about observability & debugability — compact keys are great for bytes but painful in logs/console. can we have control-plane expansion?

maria: exact thought — wire format compact, control plane/console shows expanded names. so transport-friendly but UX-friendly. also: add a `sv` (schema_version) integer to help roll forwards.

sam: example payload: 
```
{
  "p": "soft",
  "l": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z",
  "o": "rollout-service:v12",
  "h": ["canary", "low-cpu"],
  "sv": 2
}
```

kai: compatibility notes: older clients should ignore unknown short fields; servers must tolerate missing fields (default semantics: p=soft, l=null meaning indefinite until explicit eviction). we should document the defaults.

rachel: telemetry field? we want to track which subsystem observed/enforced the pin. suggest `obs` short key mapping to list of ids. not huge.

ops-bot: created INF-1234 to track RFC follow-ups and compatibility tests. (deploy-bot)

maria: decision summary: adopt compact wire schema with agreed short keys, require `sv` schema_version, and implement control-plane expansion for Console and logs. Action items: sam — draft RFC + compatibility test matrix; rachel — update Console mapping and make log-expansion helper; kai — add parsing helpers for runtime libs. i'll open serializer PR for runtime.

sam: taking the RFC, will have draft by EOD next Wednesday. link (draft): https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/9999

rachel: ack — will add Console TODO and a simple UX mock for expanded fields.

maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
